BWHP143 is the official Danish procedure code for treatment with ozanimod, which is a sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator [^src1]. This code is used within the national registry to track the clinical administration of this specific advanced therapy for patients suffering from inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) [^src1]. 

In the context of the DANIBD (Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease) database, BWHP143 is classified under the broader therapeutic umbrella of [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (biological and targeted synthetic drugs) [^src1]. Tracking this code provides essential evidence for evaluating treatment variations, patient access to advanced therapies, and overall medical practices across Denmark's hospitals, directly supporting national quality indicators [^src1]. 

According to the 2025 DANIBD report's Appendix Table 6, the actual clinical utilization of ozanimod during the audit period of October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2025, was exceptionally low [^src1]. The registry recorded zero treatments for children and only a very small number of registrations for adult patients during this one-year span [^src1].
